title: agent-budget-semantics: Differential Testing of Budget Enforcement Across AI Agent Frameworks
description: Differential testing of budget enforcement across 11 AI agent frameworks against a deterministic mock language model with a request ledger. Same underlying workload (four LLM calls, three tool calls, 800 tokens) produces four distinct gen_ai.agent.iteration_budget.consumed values across enforcing frameworks. Pre-run source-code readings agreed with runtime for exactly half of the executed frameworks. A synthetic per-iteration chargeback rate applied uniformly across the framework-reported counts diverges by up to 2.6363x (0.33834 against 0.12834 on the reference workload); the chargeback rate is a constructed pricing model rather than any vendor rate card, and the divergence is a property of the counting disagreement rather than an observed bill. The v0.5.0 software deposit description (10.5281/zenodo.22605741) gave this spread as 2.3x, which was the ratio of an illustrative worked example conflated with the measured value; see ERRATA.md entry E1 in the repository, since a minted description cannot be edited. Enforcement is measured as a mechanism rather than a boolean. Each framework was run twice against the same pinned version, once against a mock that ignores tool_choice and an absent tools array and once against one that honours both, and the mechanism is derived from per-request ledgers. openai-agents 0.22.0 stops locally and signals the provider nothing; semantic-kernel 1.44.1 withdraws tools and then declines a tool call offered anyway; agno 1.2.5 asks the provider to stop via tool_choice=none and executes whatever is returned, reaching ten model calls and nine tool calls under a declared limit of three against a non-compliant provider and holding at four and three against a conformant one. A limit whose effect depends on the counterparty cooperating is a declared limit rather than an enforced one, and a conformant counterparty makes all three mechanisms indistinguishable. Findings support recording iteration_budget.limit verbatim without cross-framework normalization; the OpenTelemetry spec PR carrying a shared iteration_budget attribute set (semantic-conventions-genai #439) was closed by its author on 2026-08-27, ninety-seven minutes after the reviewing maintainer concluded that the counts are not comparable across implementations with or without a unit travelling with them, and this work treats that negative result as the finding.
